records.name: Alliance Française de Philadelphie
records.summary: The French cultural center in Philadelphia. It teaches adults French from A1 (beginner) to C1 (advanced), and it runs French conversation meals and book clubs for adults and teens.
records.what_you_do: Take a French class at any level from A1 to C1, online or in person, join a French Tables meal to practice with native speakers, or come to a book club.

schedule.text: Adult French classes run in 10-week sessions each season, once a week for 1.5 to 2 hours, in person in Center City or online. French Tables meals and book clubs repeat on the dates listed on their event pages.

locations.label: Office (events are held at varying venues)

cost.text: Adult classes cost $375 per 10-week session, plus course materials. Individual membership is $65 and student membership (26 or younger) is $45. Members get discounts on events and can borrow from the library.

first_step.how: Open the adult classes page, pick a class at your level, and register. If you have studied French before, take the short placement test first.
first_step.basis: The adult classes page says complete beginners can check the class schedule and register, and that the placement test is for people who have studied French or spent time in a French-speaking country.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes meet once a week for 1.5 to 2 hours, with no more than 8 students, in person in Center City or online. A 10-week session costs $375 and must be paid in advance, with materials extra. The Alliance also runs French Tables meals where you practice with native speakers.
first_visit_tips: A refund needs a call to the office more than a day before the first class.
Events are held at different venues, so check the event page for the address before you go.
Sessions run each season (fall, winter, spring and summer), so pick the term that starts next.

records.notes: The adult classes page gives the levels, term dates and price. Class days and times are in two linked PDF schedules that were not read, so no days are listed. The French Tables page returned a 404, so meal details come only from the recurring events page. The Newsroom class is for intermediate and advanced learners only. The adult classes page does not say membership is required for classes. Children's classes appear in the site menu and were not opened, so kids_ok rests on that menu link.

records.name: Almanac Projects
records.summary: A dance, circus and theater company in Philadelphia that makes shows and offers free Helpful Hints workshops. It also runs AlmanAcro, an open acrobatics class on Monday evenings.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a free Helpful Hints workshop, take the Monday evening AlmanAcro acrobatics class, buy a ticket to a show, or join the mailing list.

schedule.text: AlmanAcro, an open ensemble acrobatics class, meets every Monday at 6:30 pm for 2 hours at Acro& in Northern Liberties. Free Helpful Hints workshops are offered on dates posted on the calendar.

cost.text: Helpful Hints workshops are free. AlmanAcro costs $30 with a sliding scale, and the office asks you to email if cost is a barrier. Show tickets vary by production.

access.notes: The AlmanAcro studio at Acro& is up a flight of stairs and is not ADA accessible. The site says workshop host spaces should be ADA accessible or have as few steps as possible.

first_step.how: Fill out the Airtable sign-up form linked on the site for the next free Helpful Hints workshop.
first_step.basis: The workshop is described as introductory and accessible for people of many ability levels, it is free, and sign-up is by an online form.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit lasts about 50 minutes. It starts with a 25 minute excerpt of a duet performance, then a 25 minute movement workshop that introduces dance and circus, and ends with a short question and answer. The workshops are led by Rhonda Moore and Ben Grinberg, and some are held at senior centers and other places where seniors gather.
first_visit_tips: Sign up with the Airtable form ahead of time, since the site lists sign-up rather than walk in visits.
The Oct 19 and Oct 25, 2026 workshops are at Pig Iron Theatre Company, Studio A. The Nov 7, 2026 workshop is at The Ginkgo Center.
The site does not say what to wear, so email admin@thealmanac.us if you are unsure.
For AlmanAcro, bring a water bottle, movement clothes and an optional small snack.

records.notes: Workshop dates come from the site calendar, which prints the year. The Helpful Hints page says the workshops suit seniors and are sometimes held at senior centers and homes, while the home page calls the program intergenerational for elders and young people, so kids_ok stays false from tier 1 until someone checks. The Busy People duet project is separate: it is for BIPOC elders aged 55 and up and non-elder dance artists, pays selected participants, and premieres Mar 11 to 14, 2027 at FringeArts. The tier 1 summary said the company runs festivals; no page read shows that, so the claim is removed. Pig Iron Theatre Company and The Ginkgo Center are workshop venues named on the site and were not checked as leads.

records.name: America-Italy Society of Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that links Philadelphia with Italy through Italian language courses, conversation classes, film nights, concerts and an Italian book club.
records.what_you_do: Take a 12-week Italian course or a weekly conversation class, or come to the film nights, concerts and events on its calendar. The Italian Book Club is free for members.

schedule.text: Regular Italian courses run in 12-week terms, one 90-minute class a week, in person or online. Conversation classes meet for an hour a week for 12 weeks at several levels and times. Film nights, concerts and book club meetings are listed by date on the calendar.

locations.label: Language school
locations.address: 230 S. Broad St., Suite 1105, Philadelphia, PA

cost.text: Regular courses cost $450, or $425 for members. Conversation classes cost $280 for 12 weeks. Membership is not required for courses, but the Italian Book Club is only for members.

first_step.how: On the regular courses page, click Enroll on a 101 course, the beginner level. If you are new and want a higher level, take the placement test first.
first_step.basis: The courses start at a beginner level (101) with a plain enroll button, and the conversation classes include a beginner class that starts October 14, 2026.
first_step.what_to_expect: Regular courses run 12 weeks with one 90-minute class a week, in person or online, and a course will not start with fewer than 4 students. Conversation classes meet for an hour a week for 12 weeks at beginner, pre-intermediate, intermediate and advanced levels. New students take a placement test first.
first_visit_tips: Books for levels 101 to 203 are pickup only at the school.
New students who want a level above 101 must take the placement test, and its fee comes off tuition.
Class recording is not allowed.
Call 215-735-3250 or email the front desk to choose a level before you enroll.

records.notes: The membership page does not list prices; it links to a store, so membership cost is not known from the pages read. The membership page says people aged 18 to 28 can use a separate form. The Italian Book Club meets online on selected Thursdays at 4 pm, reads contemporary Italian fiction in English translation, and is free for members only. The regular courses are in Quarter 4, 2026 (Sept 28 to Dec 19, 2026). The courses page answers the membership question: membership is not required for courses. No trial class is mentioned.

records.name: American Swedish Historical Museum
records.summary: A museum in South Philadelphia that shares Scandinavian history and culture through exhibits, events, classes, and volunteer work.
records.what_you_do: Visit the exhibits, take a family or adult education program, or volunteer for events such as Lucia Festival or Midsommarfest.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm, and closed Mondays and on major holidays. Admission is free on the second Sunday of each month.

cost.text: Adults $15, seniors, students and military $10, children 5 to 11 $5, and children under 5 free. Members are admitted free (individual membership $55, student or senior $45), and the second Sunday of each month is free for everyone.

access.notes: Accessible parking is on Pattison Avenue by the rear entrance, and caregivers of visitors with special needs do not pay admission. Service dogs are welcome, but emotional support, comfort and therapy dogs are not.

first_step.how: Visit during open hours, Tuesday to Sunday, 10 am to 4 pm. To volunteer, email the contact listed for the role you want on the volunteer page.
first_step.basis: The museum is open to visitors with posted hours and prices, and each volunteer role lists a contact to email. The page does not say whether beginners can volunteer, except that the gift shop role offers training.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit means walking through the museum's exhibits on Scandinavian history and culture during open hours. Admission is charged except for members, children under 5, and visitors on the free second Sunday of the month.
first_visit_tips: Check the hours first, since the museum is closed on Mondays and on major holidays.
Ring the doorbell at the back entrance to be let in.
Service dogs are welcome, but emotional support, comfort and therapy dogs are not.
Visit on the second Sunday of the month if you want free admission.

records.notes: The Centennial Gala is on Saturday, October 17, 2026 at 6 pm at the museum, and its registration deadline has passed, so it is not offered as a first step. The volunteer page lists roles but gives no time commitment, age minimum, background check or first shift details. The membership page lists prices but not a renewal period. No page read names a SEPTA stop, so none is listed.

records.name: Anna Crusis Feminist Choir
records.summary: A feminist choir in Philadelphia, founded in 1975, that sings songs on feminist and LGBTQ+ themes. It welcomes new singers through auditions and produces two major concerts each year.
records.what_you_do: Audition to join as a singer, come to one of the two major concerts each year, or volunteer during a concert or in another role. You can also give a donation.

schedule.text: Rehearsal days and times are not published on the site. New singers join through auditions that are announced to the newsletter list, and the choir produces two major concerts each year.

cost.text: No membership fee is listed, and donations are invited.

first_step.how: Sign up for the annacrusis.org newsletter to get the next audition details, then apply for an audition.
first_step.basis: Joining means an audition, and the next round is not posted yet. The site says audition details go out by newsletter.
first_step.what_to_expect: Your first step is an audition in Center City, Philadelphia. The 2026 round was held on July 25 and 26, and the choir announces each round to its newsletter list. ANNA also produces two major concerts each year.
first_visit_tips: The site does not say what to prepare for an audition, so ask at info@annacrusis.org or 267-825-7464 before you sign up.
Rehearsal days, times and place are not published, so ask the same way.
The choir also recruits nonsinging volunteers and board members.

records.notes: The pages disagree on the audition calendar. The home page describes the 2026 round on July 25 and 26. The auditions page still shows a 2025 notice and says applications typically open in April, with auditions in May or June, but it does not post the next round. The about page says the choir welcomes women, transgender and non-binary singers; audience.community lists women and transgender because non-binary is not a vocabulary id. The home page says all SSAA voices are welcome. Rehearsal times and locations are not on any page read.

records.name: Anne-Marie Mulgrew and Dancers Company
records.summary: A Philadelphia modern dance company, founded in 1986 by Anne-Marie Mulgrew, that makes experimental dance theater mixing dance with music, technology and art. It also teaches a free adult yoga class on Tuesday evenings at the Whitman Library.
records.what_you_do: Join the free adult yoga class on Tuesday evenings at the Whitman Library, or come to one of the company's shows, such as the Koresh Artist Showcase.

schedule.text: Free adult yoga every Tuesday, 6 to 7 pm, at the Whitman Library.

cost.text: The weekly adult yoga class at the Whitman Library is free.

first_step.how: Go to the Whitman Library at 200 Snyder Avenue on a Tuesday between 6 and 7 pm for the free adult yoga class.
first_step.basis: This is a free class for adults at a public library, listed with its day, time and place. The site does not mention a sign-up or say whether beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: The adult yoga class runs for one hour, 6 to 7 pm each Tuesday, and is taught by Anne-Marie Mulgrew, the company's artistic director. The Free Library's Whitman Branch sponsors the class, and it costs nothing to attend. The site does not say how many people come or what level the class is.
first_visit_tips: The site does not say what to wear or bring, so call 215.462.7720 or email ammdco2000@verizon.net before your first class.
The company page says it also teaches at community events in public spaces, but gives no dates, so ask before you plan around one.

records.notes: The Whitman Library class details come only from the company home page. The outreach page lists school and library workshops, master classes, partnering workshops and open rehearsals, but gives no prices, days or sign-up steps and points to the contact form. The Koresh Artist Showcase (Oct 10 and 11) appears on the home page without a year printed, so last_sign_of_life uses the June 2026 concert instead. The company page confirms the 1986 founding by Anne-Marie Mulgrew. The Free Library of Philadelphia's Whitman Branch sponsors the yoga class; no link to it was found on the pages read, so it is not listed as a lead.

records.name: Appalachian Mountain Club, Delaware Valley Chapter
records.summary: An outdoor club with about 4,500 local members that runs more than 800 hikes, paddles, bike rides, backpacking trips and trail work days a year. Most activities are free and led by trained leaders.
records.what_you_do: Join a hike, paddle or bike ride led by a trained leader, or volunteer on trail work, conservation or shelter watch.

schedule.text: Trips and events run through the year and are listed on the activities calendar. Trail crews work on an open basis, so you can join the sessions you are able to attend.

cost.text: Most activities are free. Membership dues are $50 for an individual, $75 for a family, and $25 for people under 30 or 70 and over.

first_step.how: Pick a trip on the chapter's activities calendar, register through the AMC Outdoors Connector listing, and show up. Most trips are free.
first_step.basis: Trips are open to the public, mostly free and led by trained leaders, and the 20s and 30s page says to register for an event and show up. The chapter pages do not explain trip difficulty or whether beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most trips are free and led by trained, experienced leaders. Trips run around Greater Philadelphia, the Lehigh Valley, New Jersey and Delaware, so check each listing for the meeting place. Trail crews work on an open basis, so you do not have to attend every session, and you can email the Trails Chair to learn about a crew.
first_visit_tips: The chapter pages do not explain trip difficulty, so read each listing closely before you sign up.
Sign up for the weekly email bulletin, which lists the next eight days of trips.
For trail work, ask the Trails Chair what to bring, since the page does not list tools or clothing.
The chapter's join page presents free hikes as a member benefit, so ask the chapter whether non-members can come to a first trip.

records.notes: The chapter pages do not say whether non-members can join trips. The 20s and 30s page says you do not need an AMC membership to join its trips, while the join page presents free member-led hikes as a member benefit, so the chapter should confirm. The newest dated item is the fall 2026 Footnotes newsletter, which has no month printed, so last_sign_of_life is left blank. Shelter watch volunteers are needed about once a year for the LeRoy Smith Shelter on the Appalachian Trail (about 3 to 4 hours each way). The join page footer is dated 2024 and is not used as evidence.

notes: Batch of 7 groups, all written as publish. Fetches used: 37. Alliance used 7 fetches, one more than the six per group guide; the seventh was the cultural events hub, and its French Tables page returned HTTP 404. Searches used: 0, since every gap was reachable on the group's own site. No 403s, bot checks or paywalls were met. Conflicts flagged in group notes: Anna Crusis audition timing (home page 2026 round versus an older auditions page), AMC membership wording, Almanac kids_ok (tier 1 value kept). Tier 1 summaries corrected: Almanac (festival claim removed), Anne-Marie Mulgrew (company now described from its own page), AMC (activity count and biking added), Alliance (adult classes added to what you do). Leads: none had a URL on the pages read. Named venues and partners (Pig Iron Theatre Company, The Ginkgo Center, the Free Library's Whitman Branch) were not checked.
